claim: The symplectic integrator preserves time-reversal symmetry even when the C0 geodesic trajectory crosses the origin q=0 (the C0 minimum)

experiments.label: Exp A: 0+ > 0 < x_0+   (start positive, cross origin forward)
Exp B: 0- < 0 > x_0-   (start negative, cross origin forward)
Exp D: perpendicular offset (off the q_1 axis)

verdict: CAVEAT: T-symmetry reconstruction errors are small (0.066-0.226) in all four runs, so the integrator IS time-reversible in these regimes. BUT the crossing premise never actually occurred: in every experiment the closest approach to the origin is the STARTING distance itself (idx=0), i.e. the trajectories monotonically recede from q=0. A/B/C have zero q1-axis crossings; only D crosses the axis once while keeping min dist = 0.05. The headline regime - a trajectory passing THROUGH the C0 critical point - was never exercised, so the claim is PASS-with-caveat, not confirmed.
